meaning: The number of years Methuselah lived after he fathered Lamech
description: The number 782 appears in Genesis 5:26, where it is stated that Methuselah lived seven hundred and eighty-two years after he fathered Lamech, and during this period he had other sons and daughters. Methuselah is known as the longest-lived person in the Bible, and his lifespan places him in the direct lineage from Adam to Noah. That he lived 782 years after Lamech's birth means that his life extended all the way to the year of the flood, which in Jewish tradition has given rise to reflections on God's patience and grace—that judgment was delayed as long as the righteous Methuselah was alive. Apart from this occurrence, the number has no well-established independent symbolic meaning in biblical numerology.

versions.meaning: The number 782 has no well-established or known symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: In biblical numerology and Jewish gematria, it is primarily simple numbers, certain two-digit numbers, and some specific three-digit numbers that have recognized symbolic significance. The number 782 is not mentioned as a symbolically significant number in major biblical or rabbinic sources. It can theoretically be analyzed through gematria by finding Hebrew words with the same numerical value, but it does not constitute a generally recognized symbolic number in these traditions.
versions.reason: [major] The description overlooks that the number 782 actually appears in the Bible—in Genesis 5:26 as the number of years Methuselah lived after he fathered Lamech. This is a direct biblical occurrence that should be mentioned. Stating that the number has no significance without noting this occurrence is incomplete.; [minor] The meaning field could have been more precise by mentioning that 782 is linked to Methuselah—the longest-lived person in the Bible—even though the number itself does not have an established symbolic meaning.

footnotes.text: Methuselah's total lifespan was 969 years (Gen 5:27), the highest age recorded in the Bible. With Lamech born when he was 187 and 782 years following that, Methuselah died in the year 1656 from creation—the same year as the flood according to biblical chronology.

In rabbinic tradition (Sanhedrin 108b), it is explained that God delayed the flood for seven days after Methuselah's death to observe a mourning period for the righteous, which underscores his significance in salvation history.
